newsitem.title: USA: Navistar sees lower heavy truck demand.
newsitem.headline: Navistar sees lower heavy truck demand.

text.p: Navistar International Corp., reporting significantly lower first-quarter earnings Thursday, said it expects a 13 percent reduction in industry demand for heavy trucks in the United States and Canada this year.
It said truck demand will reach 170,000 units in 1997, down 13 percent from 195,400 heavy trucks sold by the industry in 1996.
"While we have not revised our forecast, current order receipts indicate that there may be some strength beyond this level," Chairman John Horne said in a statement.
The heavy truck manufacturer also expects industry demand for medium trucks in the United States and Canada will be 112,000 units in 1997, a slight decrease from 113,200 trucks in 1996.
Navistar said it expects industry demand for school buses in fiscal 1997 to remain relatively flat year over year with the 32,500 buses sold in 1996.

Navistar reported income for the fiscal first quarter ended Jan. 31 of $15 million, or 10 cents a share, down from $22 million, or 20 cents a share a year earlier. Total sales and revenues for the quarter declined to $1.3 billion from $1.43 billion.
Navistar said its worldwide shipments of 20,400 medium and heavy trucks and school buses during the first quarter were 15.9 percent lower than a year ago.
Navistar stock was up 12.5 cents at $9.875 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
